jobs.description:
Job Description

Title:
Director, Finance (CSM)

Id:
21596

Type:
FullTime

Location:
Bolton, ON

At Husky TechnologiesTM, our success is based on your success. Our ability to keep our customers in the lead is based on building the strongest team possible.

Husky TechnologiesTM has a strong foundation built on innovation, close customer relationships and a unique culture and values. We are dedicated to offering our customers the highest quality products and services and are looking for people with the inspiration and talent to develop with us as we pursue our ambitious growth strategy. We are a leader in developing state-of-the-art technology and it is this technology base that uniquely positions us to serve customers who seek differentiation through solutions that provide speed, flexibility and maximum productivity. This capability is at the core of our mission and competitive strategy.

Husky TechnologiesTM offers a wealth of opportunity for personal growth and development. Most importantly, Husky Technologies TM offers an opportunity to work with – and be challenged by – a team of great people. Our success is possible because of the creativity, intelligence and passion of our people around the world and their desire to lead change. At the same time, we are not afraid to expect a lot and strive for leadership in all of our key markets. We are a company taking on new challenges and for the right people this means exceptional career development opportunities, the chance to be part of a team that is the best in the world at what we do and the experience that comes from working in an environment that demands constant transformation and innovation.

Husky TechnologiesTM is an exciting company with tremendous potential. We have a great team and great expectations. If you are attracted to bold goals, believe in uncompromising honesty, support mutual respect, care about environmental responsibility, have a passion for excellence and a desire to make a positive contribution – then we want you to join the Husky TechnologiesTM team!

The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of Husky’s Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. The Finance Director is expected to influence strategic decisions, lead transformation initiatives, and build a high-performing finance capability that enables the business to scale effectively.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead the annual budget, quarterly forecast, and long-range planning processes for the service business.
Develop robust revenue, margin, cost, and headcount forecasts based on operational and commercial drivers.
Translate business strategies into financial plans with clear assumptions, risks, and opportunities.
Support scenario planning and sensitivity analysis for service growth, pricing, labor utilization, and investment decisions.

Performance Management & Analysis

Deliver timely and accurate monthly financial reporting and variance analysis for service revenue, gross margin, SG&A, and operating income.
Analyze business performance by region, product line, customer segment, channel, and service offering.
Monitor and explain key drivers of performance, including labor utilization, absorption, contract profitability, attach rates, response times, and service productivity.
Provide actionable insights and recommendations to improve growth, profitability, and working capital performance.

Business Partnering

Serve as the senior finance partner to service leadership, operations, commercial teams, and Customer Success leaders, providing insight and challenge on strategic priorities, business performance, and investment decisions.
Lead financial evaluation of pricing strategies, contract renewals, service program design, and capital or operating investments to support sustainable growth and margin expansion.
Provide proactive challenge and decision support to business leaders by identifying risks, opportunities, and trade-offs across growth, productivity, service delivery, and resource allocation.
Lead cross-functional evaluation of new service offerings, business models, and transformation initiatives that improve service coverage, utilization, fulfillment, cost efficiency, and customer value.
Sponsor finance and business transformation initiatives across Finance and Customer Success Management, including enhancements to processes, reporting, operating metrics, and decision frameworks that support growth, profitability, and scalability.

Management Reporting & KPI Development

Develop and enhance dashboards, reporting tools, and KPIs that improve transparency and decision-making.
Standardize definitions and reporting for critical service metrics across the organization.
Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Process Improvement & Governance

Strengthen forecasting accuracy, reporting discipline, and financial controls within the service business.
Drive continuous improvement in FP&A processes, planning models, and reporting frameworks.
Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls
Support month-end close and planning processes in partnership with accounting and finance teams.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field required.
CPA, CMA, CFA, or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business analysis skills.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and experience with ERP and planning/reporting systems.
Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.
Proven ability to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment

Preferred Experience In a Service Business

Understanding of service revenue models such as time and materials, service contracts, preventive maintenance, subscriptions, and parts/service bundles.
Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.
Familiarity with pricing strategy, labor productivity, installed base analytics, and customer lifecycle economics

Core Competencies

Strategic leadership
Financial and commercial acumen
Analytical rigor
Executive business partnership
Influence and executive communication
Problem solving
Process improvement
Results orientation and a bias for action

Team Development

Build and lead a high-performing finance team with strong capability in financial analysis, strategic thinking, business partnership, and change leadership.
Lead, coach, and develop team members, including succession planning, capability building, and development of future finance leaders.

Financial Leadership

Provide consistent, timely, accurate, and decision-oriented financial reporting for the service business, with greater automation and self-service access to insights where possible

Husky TechnologiesTM offers a competitive compensation and benefits package and excellent opportunities for growth and advancement. We are committed to equal employment opportunity and respect, value and welcome diversity in our workplace. Husky Technologies TM also values being a great place to work and strives to maintain a safe workplace. Accordingly, Husky TechnologiesTM conditions all offers of employment on satisfactory completion of background checks.

Husky TechnologiesTM is committed to developing inclusive, barrier-free selection processes and work environments. Information received relating to accommodation measures will be addressed confidentially.

No agency or telephone inquiries please.

jobs.title: Director, Capital Markets Finance
jobs.description:
We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients.

At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute.

To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com

What You’ll Be Doing

As a Director, Capital Markets Finance, you will provide high quality reporting & advisory support to the Global Markets management team on financial and business performance, planning and forecasting. This includes reporting & analysis of the financial resources (e.g. revenue, expense, leverage, assets, liabilities, & FTE), planning and forecasting, performing/providing insights to Actual to Plan and DFE to GL variance analysis, and assessing the financial performance and developing financial plan for initiatives. This role will support Global Equities desks in Global Markets. It is an individual contributor role.

At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. You’ll have the flexibility to manage your work activities within a hybrid work arrangement where you’ll spend 1-3 days per week on-site, while other days will be remote.

How You’ll Succeed

Reporting & analysis – Review daily, weekly, monthly and quarterly financial results and provide high quality, insightful and timely analysis of financial performance for Global Markets businesses. Identify opportunities for cost savings and support the effective management of Balance Sheet, Funding/Liquidity and Capital Resources (RWA, Leverage and Regulatory Capital). Ensure that reporting and analysis keep pace with the changing business and environment.
Planning and forecasting – Coordinate and support the development of the financial strategic and business plans for Global Markets. Work closely with business heads, Risk and Capital Management, to ensure reasonableness of market assumptions and impact of expected regulatory changes to ensure successful execution. Understand and review allocations to the business and be able to work closely with the counterparts in other areas of the bank to challenge allocations and ensure they are reasonable.
Business initiatives - Work closely with the business leader to provide sound financial advice on strategic and tactical initiatives and projects. Provide leadership, accountability and facilitate the implementation of business optimization/process reengineering, and strategic initiatives impacted supported businesses.
Collaboration - Establish and build healthy working relations and partnerships with the business leaders in Global Markets, as well as peers in Risk Management, Operations, Technology, Treasury and other areas of Finance.

Who You Are

You can demonstrate a minimum of 5 years experience in a Finance role, have a professional accounting designation and/or a post graduate business degree; good financial accounting knowledge and the ability to comprehend complex accounting issues and summarize them for the business; strong problem solving, analytical, judgment and change implementation capabilities.
You act like an owner. You thrive when you're empowered to take the lead, go above and beyond, and deliver results.
You're passionate about people. You find meaning in relationships, and surround yourself with a diverse network of partners. You build trust through respect and authenticity
You're driven by collective success. You know that collaboration can transform a good idea into a great one. You understand the power of an inclusive team that enjoys working together to bring a shared vision to life.
You give meaning to data. You enjoy investigating complex problems, and making sense of information. You're confident in your ability to communicate detailed information in an impactful way.
You live your values. You bring high standards, genuine care to your relationships, and want to grow with an employer that shares your values and brings out your best.

What CIBC Offers

At CIBC, your goals are a priority. We start with your strengths and ambitions as an employee and strive to create opportunities to tap into your potential. We aspire to give you a career, rather than just a paycheck.

We work to recognize you in meaningful, personalized ways including a competitive salary, incentive pay, banking benefits, a benefits program*, defined benefit pension plan*, an employee share purchase plan, a vacation offering, wellbeing support, and MomentMakers, our social, points-based recognition program.
Our spaces and technological toolkit will make it simple to bring together great minds to create innovative solutions that make a difference for our clients.
We cultivate a culture where you can express your ambition through initiatives like Purpose Day; a paid day off dedicated for you to use to invest in your growth and development.
Subject to plan and program terms and conditions

What You Need To Know

CIBC is committed to creating an inclusive environment where all team members and clients feel like they belong. We seek applicants with a wide range of abilities and we provide an accessible candidate experience. If you need accommodation, please contact Mailbox.careers-carrieres@cibc.com
CIBC is committed to clarity in our hiring process. All roles posted are opportunities we’re actively recruiting for, unless stated otherwise.
You need to be legally eligible to work at the location(s) specified above and, where applicable, must have a valid work or study permit.
We may ask you to complete an attribute-based assessment and other skills test (such as simulation, coding, French proficiency).
We use artificial intelligence tools during the recruitment process. Our goal for the application process is to get to know more about you, all that you have to offer, and give you the opportunity to learn more about us.

jobs.title: VP Finance
jobs.description:
En tant que vice-président(e) finances vous dirigez les activités financières afin d'éclairer les décisions de l'entreprise dans le secteur des technologies et télécommunications. Vous assurez une vision claire de la performance financière et des priorités du département Comptabilité et finances.
Informations sur l'entreprise

Notre client évolue dans le secteur des logiciels et technologies.
Missions

En tant que vice-président(e) finances, vous prenez en charge les responsabilités suivantes :

1. Structurer et faire évoluer la fonction Finance
- Concevoir l'architecture du département finance global : recruter, encadrer et fidéliser des talents de haut niveau.
- Moderniser l'écosystème technologique : auditer, sélectionner et déployer des modules ERP alimentés par l'IA, des solutions de rapprochement automatisé et des outils de prévision prédictive.
- Mettre en place des contrôles internes robustes, des SOP et des politiques comptables harmonisées à l'international.
2. Gérer les transactions intercompagnies internationales
- Optimiser les prix de transfert et superviser la documentation associée entre filiales.
- Encadrer les risques de change multidevises par des stratégies de couverture et l'optimisation de la trésorerie globale.
- Assurer la conformité fiscale transfrontalière avec des fiscalistes externes : nexus, optimisation des structures fiscales internationales.
3. Intégrer l'IA et l'automatisation
- Piloter la transition des processus manuels vers des flux assistés par l'IA (comptes fournisseurs, comptes clients, clôtures mensuelles).
- Déployer l'analytique prédictive et des outils BI alimentés par l'IA pour les prévisions de revenus, la planification par scénarios et l'analyse des écarts.
- Développer les compétences de l'équipe (prompt engineering, analyse de données, automatisation) et instaurer une culture d'adoption technologique.
4. Diriger la stratégie financière et la reddition de comptes
- Présenter les états financiers mensuels et annuels, les tableaux de bord KPI et les présentations au comité exécutif, au conseil et aux investisseurs.
- Superviser budgets, prévisions glissantes et modèles d'allocation du capital pour l'expansion internationale et l'évolution des produits.
- Appuyer le développement corporatif : modélisation financière, diligence raisonnable et intégration pour levées de fonds et fusions-acquisitions.
Profil du candidat

Expérience professionnelle
- 10+ ans d'expérience progressive en finance, dont 3+ ans dans un rôle de direction senior (VP, Directeur(trice), Head of Finance) au sein d'une entreprise SaaS/technologique financée par VC/PE.
- Expérience avérée de gestion multi-entités et multi-juridictions, devises étrangères et prix de transfert.
- Succès démontré dans la création ou la transformation d'un département finance en contexte de forte croissance.
Compétences techniques et IA
- Maîtrise d'ERP globaux modernes (NetSuite, Workday, Microsoft Dynamics 365) et d'outils de consolidation financière.
- Expérience ou forte capacité d'adoption des flux IA/automatisation : rapprochement automatisé, recherche financière par LLM, pipelines de données, capture OCR.

Formation et certifications
- Baccalauréat en finance, comptabilité, économie ou domaine connexe.
- Titre CPA, CFA ou MBA fortement considéré comme un atout.
Compétences humaines
- Leader du changement, adaptable, capable d'adopter les technologies disruptives et de mobiliser les équipes.
- Communicateur(trice) stratégique apte à traduire des données financières complexes pour parties prenantes non techniques.
- Esprit analytique axé sur la scalabilité, l'intégrité des données et l'efficacité opérationnelle.

Conditions et Avantages

- Environnement de travail flexible (télétravail/hybride) - 1 à 2 déplacement par mois à Mirabel.
- Salaire de base entre 170 000 et 190 000$ CAD
- Culture collaborative.
- Assurance collective complète (santé, dentaire, paramédical).
- REER avec contribution employeur (Québec).
- Allocation bien-être annuelle.
- Cadeau d'anniversaire.
- Allocation Internet mensuelle.
- Vacances et congés payés compétitifs.

MPI ne fait pas de discrimination fondée sur la race, la religion, le sexe, l'orientation sexuelle, l'identité ou l'expression du genre, l'âge, le handicap, l'état civil, ou sur le statut d'un individu dans un groupe ou une classe quelconque autrement protégé par la législation applicable en matière de droits de l'homme. jobs.title: Director, Finance
jobs.description:
Thank you for contacting the Government of Nunavut.

Please do not send sensitive or personal information, including (but not limited to): social insurance numbers, birthdates, information of other people, or health information. Please only send a brief description of your issue or concern and how we can contact you. We will make sure the correct person contacts you if they need more information or if they can answer your question or concern.

This employment opportunity is open to all applicants. Applicants must be currently eligible to work in Canada.

An eligibility list may be created to fill future vacancies.

As this is a term position ending June 2028, current indeterminate Government of Nunavut employees may be offered a competitive transfer assignment for the duration of the term if they are deemed to be the successful candidate, however this is subject to managerial approval.

Reporting to the Executive Director, Corporate Services, the Director, Finance (Director) is the senior financial advisor for the Department of Health. The position is responsible for the financial stewardship and accountability of public funds administered by Health. At the core of their duties is the oversight of the department’s capital and operations and maintenance budget, ensuring that financial resources are allocated efficiently and in accordance with government policies and regulations. The Director of Finance is also accountable for compliance with financial regulations and standards. They must ensure that all financial transactions and operations within the department adhere to the Financial Administrative Manual (FAM) as well as legal and ethical guidelines.

The main responsibilities of the Director are, but are not limited to:

Leading the process of developing the department's annual budget, working with program managers and finance staff to gather input, projections, and cost estimates;
Facilitating the budget approval process, working closely with government agencies, legislative bodies, and stakeholders to address questions, concerns, and revisions;
Overseeing the allocation and execution of budgeted funds, ensuring that expenditures are in line with approved allocations and regulatory guidelines;
Managing the process for budget amendments or revisions as necessary, providing clear justifications and seeking necessary approvals for changes;
Ensuring that all financial reports meet regulatory requirements and government accounting principles, providing transparency and accountability in financial disclosures;
Establishing and maintaining robust internal controls to safeguard financial assets, prevent fraud, and ensure the accuracy and integrity of financial data;
Overseeing and leading a team of financial professionals, providing guidance, mentorship, and support to promote their professional growth and ensure effective departmental operations;
Fostering a culture of collaboration and cross-functional teamwork, working closely with other department heads to ensure financial considerations are integrated into broader strategic planning.

The knowledge, skills, and abilities required for this job are usually obtained through a recognized:

Undergraduate degree in accounting, finance, business administration, economics, commerce, or related field;
Completion of a professional accounting designation CPA (CMA, CGA or CA);
Eight (8) years of related experience;
Five (5) years of progressive managerial experience in assigning priorities and managing performance of professional teams.

This is a Position of Trust and a satisfactory Criminal Record Check is required.

The Official Languages of Nunavut are Inuktut, English and French. Applicants may submit their resume in any of the official languages of Nunavut. Fluency in more than one of Nunavut’s official languages would be considered an asset. Knowledge of Inuit communities, culture, land, Inuit Qaujimajatuqangit, Inuktut and experience working in a northern cross-cultural environment are also considered assets.

Acceptable combinations of education and experience may be considered for this position. We encourage you to apply if you have equivalent years of education and/or experience equal to the education and experience requirements listed above.

The Government of Nunavut is committed to creating a representative workforce; therefore, priority will be given to Nunavut Inuit who self-identify as being enrolled under the Nunavut Agreement in accordance with the Priority Hiring Policy.
Government of Nunavut employees serving a probationary period must obtain and provide written authorization from the deputy head of their employing department. The authorization from the deputy head must accompany your application for your application to be considered.
Possession of a criminal record may not disqualify candidates from being considered. An assessment of the criminal record will be measured against the scope and duties of the position. This is only a requirement for positions that require a satisfactory criminal record or vulnerable sector check.
Applicants may submit their resume in any of the Official Languages of Nunavut.
Only those candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

The onus is on candidates in receipt of foreign post-secondary education credentials to have their foreign credentials assessed through a recognized Canadian education institution. Failure to do so may result in the rejection of their application.

jobs.title: Director of Pricing and Business Analytics
jobs.description:
About The Role

GFL is seeking a visionary, high-energy leader with a passion for financial modeling, advanced analytics, and commercial business insights. Are you a strategic leader who thrives at the intersection of complex data, technology, and executive strategy? As the Director of Business Analytics, you will drive our enterprise-wide intelligence roadmap and foster a high-impact, data-driven culture across our fast-paced, high-growth organization.

This is a newly created position driven by our consistent expansion, appetite for data-driven decision-making, and relentless push for continuous improvement. You will join our leadership team at an exceptionally exciting time as we’ve embarked on our pricing program transformation, placing you at the forefront of this value creating engagement. Working with a "no can't do" attitude, you will translate complex technical data into compelling commercial narratives that shape global corporate strategy and optimize bottom-line performance.

Key Responsibilities

Reporting directly to the VP, Operations Strategy, you will lead a dynamic team to drive performance and deliver value-added decision support across the business. Key responsibilities include:

Pricing Excellence: Assess enterprise pricing performance, build advanced pricing models from scratch, identify margin opportunities, and challenge assumptions. Influence Area Vice Presidents and Business Unit leaders to translate analytical insights into actionable strategies that optimize commercial outcomes.
Advanced Analytics & AI: Champion statistical modeling, machine learning, and predictive analytics to transition the business from descriptive reporting to prescriptive intelligence. Accelerate speed-to-insight by integrating modern analytics tools, AWS-native workflows, predictive machine learning, and responsible GenAI/copilots.
Strategic Roadmap Development: Define and execute the long-term vision for the Business Analytics department. Scale enterprise data platforms and ensure full alignment between analytics initiatives and global corporate objectives.
Operational Excellence: Oversee the full data lifecycle—from ingestion and pipeline collaboration to the delivery of interactive executive dashboards, automated workflows, and high-impact predictive tools.
Data Governance & Integrity: Establish rigorous standards for data quality, security, and governance. Define control frameworks and KPIs to ensure business intelligence is accurate, reliable, and meeting compliance benchmarks.
Stakeholder Influence: Partner closely with Operations, Sales, Marketing, and Finance leadership. Translate ambiguous operational and market questions into clear recommendations, guiding executive partners through trade-offs with decision-ready narratives.
Team Leadership: Hire, coach, and retain a high-performing team of analysts and data professionals. Foster a culture of continuous improvement, analytical rigor, and collaborative business partnering.

Qualifications

10+ years of progressive experience in analytics, data science, or related quantitative fields, including experimentation frameworks, statistical modeling, and time-series analysis.
5+ years in pricing, revenue management, or applied data science within B2B or service-oriented industries, with a proven track record of building dynamic pricing and financial models from scratch.
5+ years of people management experience, including structuring team processes for service delivery in fast-paced environments, presenting to C-suite audiences, and driving cross-functional alignment.
Expert-level modeling skills and hands-on proficiency with major BI tools (Power BI, QuickSight, Tableau) and database querying (SQL).
Direct experience with AWS cloud data environments (e.g., S3, Glue, Athena, Forecast, or SageMaker) and leveraging GenAI/copilots to accelerate insight generation.
Executive Communication & Influence: Exceptional ability to distill complex data insights into concise, persuasive presentations for senior leaders.
Commercial & Financial Acumen: Deep understanding of operational finance, FP&A, and business operations, with the ability to link data metrics directly to bottom-line profitability.
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Finance, Economics, Statistics, or Computer Science required; Master’s degree in a quantitative field highly preferred.

Job Description

Director, Enterprise Applications

Be bold. Think bigger. Create lasting impact.

At Peel Region, technology enables the essential public services our communities rely on every day.

Reporting to the Chief Information Officer, the Director, Enterprise Applications
will shape Peel’s enterprise technology direction and lead the modernization and sustainable operation of critical platforms, including SAP S/4HANA, SAP Concur and IBM Maximo Enterprise Asset Management.

This is an opportunity to lead meaningful business transformation and strengthen systems supporting approximately 7,000 users across Peel Region.

The opportunity

You will connect technology investments with Peel’s strategic priorities, service outcomes and future needs. Working with senior leaders, business teams and external partners, you will lead enterprise application strategy, major implementations, governance, operational sustainment and organizational adoption.

Your leadership will ensure Peel’s enterprise applications are integrated, reliable and positioned to deliver lasting value for employees, services and the community.

Advancing Peel’s strategic priorities

Peel’s Strategic Plan Sets The Direction For Building a Community For Life
. This Role Will Contribute Particularly To Service Excellence, Our People And Future Ready
By:

Modernizing the systems that enable essential public services.
Improving the technology experience for employees and leaders.
Strengthening data, reporting and enterprise decision-making.
Establishing sustainable application support and governance models.
Supporting responsible stewardship of public resources.
Helping employees successfully adopt new technology and ways of working.

Learn more about the Peel Region Strategic Plan .

What You Will Do

Lead Peel’s Enterprise Applications Strategy and Roadmap.
Provide strategic leadership for SAP S/4HANA, SAP Concur, IBM Maximo and other critical enterprise applications.
Oversee complex implementation, modernization, integration and sustainment initiatives.
Align technology investments with service priorities, user needs and measurable organizational benefits.
Establish governance, service standards, service-level agreements and sustainable support models.
Maintain stable operations while leading the transition to modern solutions.
Lead organizational change through stakeholder engagement, business readiness, communications, training and adoption.
Manage procurement, implementation partners, strategic suppliers, contracts, budgets, deliverables and vendor performance.
Identify enterprise risks, resolve complex issues and provide clear advice to senior leaders.
Build trusted relationships across business and technology functions.
Lead and develop a multidisciplinary team that values accountability, collaboration and professional growth.

What You Bring

A relevant postgraduate degree, preferably in Business, Computer Science, Information Technology or a related discipline.
SAP Certified Application Associate and/or SAP Certified Development Associate certification.
Project Management Professional (PMP) certification.
At least eight years of experience implementing enterprise applications in a complex public-sector environment.
A satisfactory Level 2 Criminal Record Check obtained directly from a police station (third-party background checks will not be accepted).
Implementation and operational experience with SAP S/4HANA and SAP Concur and/or IBM Maximo Enterprise Asset Management.
Experience leading large-scale technology implementations across multiple business functions and stakeholder groups.
Strong knowledge and practical application of formal project management methodologies.
Experience managing procurement, implementation partners, contracts, budgets, deliverables and vendor performance.
Experience establishing governance, service standards, service-level agreements and operational support models.
Strong strategic thinking, change leadership, risk management and relationship-building skills.
An understanding of government structures, political considerations and Council-level accountability.

How You Will Demonstrate Peel’s Values

Inclusion: Engage diverse perspectives to create accessible, user-centred enterprise solutions.
Transparency: Establish clear governance and communicate openly about decisions, progress, risks, costs and results.
Care and Support: Lead change with empathy and help employees confidently adopt new technology.
Collaboration: Bring business, technology and external partners together around shared outcomes.
Leadership: Set a clear direction, make accountable decisions, develop people and champion innovation and continuous improvement.

Why work at Peel?

At Peel, you can lead, impact and grow
while helping shape better communities and build a Community for Life
.

You Will Join An Inclusive And Values-led Organization Where Employees Are Encouraged To Be Bold, Think Bigger And Contribute Meaningfully. In This Role, You Will Have The Opportunity To:

Shape Peel’s enterprise applications strategy and future technology roadmap.
Lead transformation across critical business platforms.
Influence decisions that strengthen services and organizational performance.
Improve the technology experience for employees and leaders.
Develop people and build future organizational capability.
Make a lasting contribution to responsive and sustainable public service.

The Peel Employee Experience

As an eligible employee, you will receive:

Comprehensive health, dental and vision benefits, including psychological health supports, effective on your first day.
Automatic enrolment in the OMERS pension plan.
Five weeks of annual vacation accrued monthly.
Three paid personal days, in addition to floating holidays.
Flexible work hours that support well-being and work-life integration.
An inclusive workplace culture grounded in collaborative leadership and meaningful public service.

Join us.

Enterprise applications are more than technology platforms. They enable our employees, strengthen public services and help Peel respond to changing community needs.

jobs.title: Director, AI Wealth Enablement
jobs.description:
Permanent Full Time

As the Director, AI Wealth Enablement you will be responsible for enabling the effective, responsible, and value driven adoption of Artificial Intelligence in support AI use case implementation within the Wealth business. This role partners with business leaders to identify, shape, and validate AI opportunities, translating business needs into clear AI use cases. Also working closely with Technology to ensure solutions are feasible, prioritized, and deliver measurable value. A key component of the role will be engaging with Advisors directly to gather feedback on use cases and educate on AI capabilities. The Director will operate as an enabler and will partner with leaders in all functional areas to accelerate the business strategy using AI – this includes opportunity identification, business case development, prioritization, and value realization. Success in this role will be measured by AI driven value realization across Wealth, which will be achieved through influence, strong stakeholder relationships, and a deep understanding of both business outcomes and AI capabilities

What you will do:

Partner with functional leaders to identify high value opportunities where AI can improve outcomes and efficiency as related to advisor experience, dealer processes, compliance needs, and other wealth opportunities
Work with business leaders to unpack and shape AI business cases, clarifying the problem to solve, expected benefits, risks, and success measures before solutions are pursued
Establish channels to engage directly with advisors; gather feedback to form as requirements to solve advisor productivity and complexity issues using AI, while also being an advocate for existing and emerging AI capabilities that advisors should be adopting
As part of business architecture align with existing mandate to translate business needs into clear AI use cases and requirements, partnering with technology, data, and architecture teams to prioritize, assess feasibility, and alignment to enterprise AI capabilities and standards
Build AI literacy and proficiency across leadership teams by sharing insights, patterns, and practical examples of what is working, and what is not, across the organization
Measure and track value realization from use cases
Champion responsible AI practices, ensuring compliance with privacy, security, and ethical standards
Stay current on AI trends, emerging technologies, and competitor offerings

What you will bring:

Deep understanding of AI capabilities and limitations (including generative AI, automation, analytics, and machine learning) and how they apply in regulated environments such as financial service, inclusive of wealth
Strong ability to bridge business strategy and technology, translating business problems into actionable AI opportunities and explaining AI concepts in clear, practical terms
Experience with engaging stakeholders in the field; advisors, and/or advisor support teams
Demonstrated experience developing, assessing, and prioritizing business cases, including benefits realization and outcome measurement
Demonstrated ability to lead through influence and drive cross-functional outcomes across business and technology stakeholders
Exceptional stakeholder leadership and partnership skills, with confidence engaging senior business, compliance, and technology leaders
Strong judgment and systems thinking, balancing innovation with risk, governance, and long-term sustainability
Excellent communication and problem-solving skills
Passion for innovation, with a track record of challenging the status quo and embracing change in AI adoption
Learning mindset with ability to experiment, embrace learnings, and pivot quickly

The base salary for this position is between $128,200 - $178,200
annually. This represents base salary only and does not represent other variable compensation components of our total compensation ( i.e. annual bonus, commission etc). If you are selected to move forward in our recruitment process, your recruiter will be able to discuss additional details of our total rewards program with you.

Career opportunities will be open a minimum of 5 business days from the date of posting, closing dates will vary depending on the search activity. All applications received will be reviewed on a rolling basis.

jobs.title: Director of Digital
jobs.description:
Who We Are:

ACAMS is the global leader in certification, training, and intelligence for anti-financial crime (AFC) professionals. ACAMS sets the standard for how organizations prevent, detect, and respond to money laundering, fraud and sanctions evasion. Trusted by 70% of the world's leading banks, as well as governmental and law enforcement agencies, and FinTechs, the organization has 120,000+ members across 200+ countries and territories. Its 65+ chapters and annual conferences connect AFC professionals across every major financial center. Learn more at acams.org.

Opportunity at a Glance

The Director of Digital owns the strategy, roadmap, and ongoing delivery of ACAMS.org and the broader ACAMS Digital Ecosystem. This is more than a website leadership role: our digital platform is a product in its own right, spanning discovery, trial, purchase, and renewal of certifications, training, membership, and subscription-based news and intelligence content. You will act as the connective tissue between Marketing, Product, Sales, Operations, and News/Intelligence — translating business goals into a prioritized backlog and shipping continuously through an agile delivery process.

Responsibilities

Develop and maintain the roadmap for ACAMS.org, with stakeholder buy-in, spanning the full Digital Lifecycle: Find, Try, Buy, Renew, and Consume
Play a leading role in defining the product vision for the ACAMS Digital Ecosystem — an end-to-end digital experience supporting ACAMS members across their professional journeys, from first certification through ongoing intelligence and community engagement
Drive stakeholder alignment across Marketing, Product, Sales, Operations, and News/Intelligence divisions to maintain a unified backlog and prioritize website changes against business impact
Own the ongoing release of website enhancements and bug fixes through an agile delivery process, partnering with engineering, design, and vendor teams on sprint planning, QA, and launch
Optimize the digital commerce and subscription experience — conversion, self-service, and renewal — for products including premium news and intelligence content
Define and track KPIs for digital performance (traffic, conversion, engagement, retention) and use data and user research to inform prioritization
Lead and participate in regular executive updates on roadmap progress, results, and risks

Qualifications

8–10+ years in digital product management, digital experience, or e-commerce leadership, including ownership of a revenue-generating website or digital platform
Proven success managing a cross-functional backlog and shipping through agile processes (Scrum/Kanban) with internal teams and external partners
Experience with subscription, membership, or premium content business models; familiarity with CMS, e-commerce, CRM, and analytics platforms
Strong stakeholder management and executive communication skills — able to build consensus across divisions with competing priorities
Data-driven decision-maker comfortable with web analytics, A/B testing, and customer journey optimization
Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree or product management certification a plus. Familiarity with professional associations, credentialing, or B2B publishing environments is a strong plus

EEO

We are proud to be an EEO employer M/F/D/V. At ACAMS, we welcome everyone and have a strong commitment towards diversity and inclusion. We encourage our Colleagues to be their true authentic selves and support laws that prohibit discrimination everywhere we do business. We also maintain a drug-free workplace.

jobs.title: Head of Digital Performance
jobs.description:
About The Lacroix Medical Group

A leader in private medicine in Quebec, the Lacroix Medical Group
comprises three rapidly growing divisions:

Medical Clinics
Operating Rooms
Biomedical Laboratory

Since its founding in 2009, the Lacroix Medical Group has experienced sustained growth and now has nearly 350 employees across its various divisions. Driven by an ambitious and entrepreneurial vision, the organization continues its expansion across the province and aspires to accelerate its development in national and international markets.

OUR MISSION

To be the benchmark in private healthcare.

OUR VALUES

Passion | Respect | Integrity | Commitment | Innovation

Mandate

Reporting to the Director of Marketing, the Digital Performance Manager
plays a key role in the growth, reach, and success of the Lacroix Medical Group.

Passionate about digital marketing, data, and innovation, this individual leverages their expertise to develop high-performing strategies that generate a tangible impact on our business objectives. Their daily challenge: transforming data into opportunities, strategies into results, and ideas into measurable actions. In a dynamic environment encompassing multiple clinics, services, and business lines, the successful candidate will lead the organization's overall digital performance. They will develop, deploy, measure, and optimize digital media campaigns to increase our visibility, generate business opportunities, and maximize the return on our marketing investments. A true strategic partner to internal teams, this proactive individual will work closely with various stakeholders to understand their challenges, identify the best growth opportunities, and recommend innovative, results-oriented solutions. Thanks to her expertise, she actively contributes to the evolution of our digital maturity, the continuous improvement of our practices, and the achievement of our growth ambitions. Curious, analytical, and always on the lookout for new trends, the Digital Performance Manager enjoys experimenting, innovating, and pushing boundaries. Whether through campaign optimization, advanced data analytics, artificial intelligence, geolocation, or new approaches to digital marketing, this individual helps maintain the Lacroix Medical Group's position among the most innovative organizations in its sector. If you are performance-driven, thrive on challenges, and want to grow in an environment where your ideas will have a concrete and measurable impact, this position is for you. Your Role Take charge of the activation, management, and analysis of digital media campaigns (SEM, programmatic, and social media). Ensure the implementation of trafficking, online deployment, execution, daily bid monitoring, campaign health, and performance analysis. Manage and ensure adherence to media budgets while optimizing ROI. investments. Support internal clients, understand their needs, advise them, and recommend the best digital strategies. Ensure rigorous monitoring of conversions, data quality, and overall campaign performance. In-depth analysis of results, identify optimization opportunities, and share learnings with team members. Effectively navigate between multiple projects, brands, and priorities simultaneously. Manage and optimize Google Ads and Meta Ads campaigns to achieve established performance objectives. Utilize measurement and optimization tools such as Google Analytics 4, Google Search Console, and SEMrush. Design, maintain, and analyze performance dashboards in Looker Studio. Constantly monitor best practices in Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) and Search Engine Optimization (SEO). Participate to the development, implementation, and execution of digital strategies with the team's various experts. Identify and recommend new acquisition, conversion, and optimization opportunities to support the organization's growth.

The Ideal Candidate

Bachelor's degree in marketing, communications, or a related field.
Minimum of 6 to 8 years of experience in digital marketing and performance campaign management.
Experience in an environment encompassing multiple divisions, brands, or business lines.
Agency experience (a significant asset).
Valid Google Ads certification.
Excellent command of Google Ads, Meta Ads, Google Analytics 4, and Looker Studio.
Experience with other platforms and tools, including Google Tag Manager and TikTok Ads Manager.
Strong analytical skills and a strong results orientation.
Highly autonomous, rigorous, and organized.
Initiative and ability to thrive in a constantly evolving environment.
Ability to manage multiple priorities in a context of rapid growth.
Excellent command of both spoken and written French and English.
Strong interest in innovation, artificial intelligence, and the evolution of digital technologies.

Our Benefits

Lacroix Gift Card of $500 per year, including fast access to a doctor.
Annual Health Account of $1,100, which can reach $2,000 based on years of service. FTQ Workers' Fund with employer contribution. Annual budget dedicated to continuing education. Real opportunities for career advancement and professional development. Three weeks of vacation upon hiring. Four paid floating holidays per year. Hybrid work model. Free parking. Modern, bright, and collaborative work environment. Unlimited coffee and employee lounge. Join an ambitious, growing organization where your expertise, ideas, and passion will directly contribute to shaping the future of private healthcare. Quebec.
